review_evidence: README states the project goal is to prove Fermat’s Last Theorem for regular primes in Lean.
The hydrated snapshot has 27 Lean files with dozens of theorems and more than one hundred lemmas covering both Case I and Case II.
FltRegular/CaseI/Statement.lean contains the main reduction and case-I theorem chain, while the CaseII modules develop ideal/cyclotomic arguments; this is direct mathematical formalization prior art.
summary: Retain flt-regular as the Lean formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem for regular primes.

summary: Surveyed all 16 files (FltRegular.lean root, FltRegular/{CaseI,CaseII,NumberTheory,SmallNumbers}) with wc -c and a declaration-keyword grep. Read completely FltRegular.lean, FltRegular/FltRegular.lean, NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Rat.lean, NumberTheory/RegularPrimes.lean, CaseII/Statement.lean, SmallNumbers/Five/FLT5.lean, SmallNumbers/Seven/FLT7.lean, and the first 60 lines of NumberTheory/Hilbert92.lean. Fifteen files hold Lean declarations and proofs of the FLT-for-regular-primes development (flt_regular, caseI/caseII, IsRegularPrime, Hilbert 92/94, Kummer's lemma, FLT5/FLT7). FltRegular.lean is an import-only root module with a doc comment; under FILTER-007 it stays primary-eligible because removal needs an end-to-end verified auxiliary navigation path, which this review did not establish. Disposition: retain all.

summary: All 12 files in this review unit contain substantial formal mathematical content — definitions, lemmas, theorems, and proofs — directly contributing to the FLT-for-regular-primes development. The files cover Case I and Case II of FLT, cyclotomic ideal factorization, Hilbert 92, Kummer's lemma, principal ideal criteria for cyclotomic fields, and concrete FLT proofs for exponents 5 and 7. None are pure import aggregators (FILTER-007), none lack formal declarations (FILTER-004), and no content-invariant justifies hard exclusion (FILTER-021). The default disposition under FILTER-025 is retain.
